title: Abelian sheaves killed by n are the sheaves of Z/n-modules
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme, $T_{\Et}$ its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], $n\ge1$ an integer, $(\mathbf Z/n)_T$ the constant sheaf of rings with value $\mathbf Z/n$ on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], $\Mod(T_{\Et},\mathbf Z/n)$ the category of sheaves of $(\mathbf Z/n)_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and $\mathrm{forget}:\Mod(T_{\Et},\mathbf Z/n)\to\Ab(T_{\Et})$ the functor to abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] forgetting the module structure. Then: (1) for every sheaf $G$ of $(\mathbf Z/n)_T$-modules, $n\cdot\mathrm{id}=0$ on the abelian sheaf $\mathrm{forget}(G)$; (2) for every abelian sheaf $F$ with $n\cdot\mathrm{id}_F=0$ there is exactly one structure of sheaf of $(\mathbf Z/n)_T$-modules on $F$ extending its structure of abelian sheaf, and in it the image $\iota_U(\bar a)\in(\mathbf Z/n)_T(U)$ of the constant $\bar a\in\mathbf Z/n$ (with $\iota$ the canonical map from the constant presheaf to its sheafification) acts on $F(U)$ as multiplication by any integer $a$ lifting $\bar a$; (3) for sheaves $G,G'$ of $(\mathbf Z/n)_T$-modules, every morphism of abelian sheaves $\mathrm{forget}(G)\to\mathrm{forget}(G')$ is $(\mathbf Z/n)_T$-linear. Hence $\mathrm{forget}$ is fully faithful, and its image is the full subcategory of abelian sheaves killed by $n$; in particular an isomorphism of abelian sheaves between two sheaves of $(\mathbf Z/n)_T$-modules is an isomorphism of sheaves of $(\mathbf Z/n)_T$-modules. (Ingredients: every section of $(\mathbf Z/n)_T$ over $U$ is, on some etale covering of $U$, the image of constants $\bar a_i$; a unital additive action of $\bar a$ is multiplication by $a$; separation of $F$. Existence in (2): the action of the constant presheaf $\mathbf Z/n$ on $F$ by $\bar a\cdot s=as$ is well defined because $nF=0$ and extends along the sheafification of the constant presheaf of rings, sheafification preserving finite products.)

source.place: Definition 03RW (definition-constructible), parts (2) and (3), and the proof of Theorem 03SC, where Stacks passes between abelian sheaves killed by n and sheaves of Z/n-modules without comment; the module notion is that of Modules on Sites (sites-modules.tex, definition of O-modules). Not stated in Stacks; agent-formulated.

proof.text: Put $P(U)=\mathbf Z/n$ with identity restrictions and $\mathcal O=(\mathbf Z/n)_T$. By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] the canonical map $\eta:P\to\mathcal O$ is sheafification in rings, hence every $\eta_U$ is a unital ring map. For any sheaf $G$ of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], any $a\in\mathbf Z$, and $s\in G(U)$, one has $\eta_U(\bar a)=a\cdot1_{\mathcal O(U)}$ and $\eta_U(\bar a)s=as$ by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-zmod-module-structure-killed-by-n]. Taking $a=n$ gives $ns=\eta_U(0)s=0$. This proves (1) and the prescribed action of constants in (2). In particular, restriction of scalars along $\eta$ recovers the usual $\mathbf Z/n$-action on every underlying group of sections.

proof.text: Let $F$ be an abelian sheaf with $n\,\mathrm{id}_F=0$. This equality is sectionwise, so $nF(U)=0$ for every $U$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-zmod-module-structure-killed-by-n] gives $\bar a\cdot s=as$ on $F(U)$. Every restriction map is additive and hence $\mathbf Z/n$-linear by clause (4) of that node. These structures therefore define a presheaf of $P$-modules: its underlying additive presheaf is $F$, with the same restrictions. The identity $F\to F$ is a sheafification as an abelian presheaf, because every map from $F$ to an abelian sheaf factors uniquely through this identity [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] with its ring presheaf $\mathcal O$ equal to $P$, its ring sheafification equal to our $\mathcal O$, its module presheaf equal to $F$, and its abelian sheafification map equal to $\mathrm{id}_F$. It gives an $\mathcal O$-action on the very same abelian sheaf $F$. Compatibility with $P\times F\to F$ says precisely $\eta_U(\bar a)s=as$. Thus the required module structure exists, with no replacement of the underlying abelian sheaf.

proof.text: For uniqueness in (2), any other sheaf-of-$\mathcal O$-modules structure on the fixed abelian sheaf $F$ has, by step 1, action $\eta_U(\bar a)s=as$. Its action map is a map of sheaves of sets $\mathcal O\times F\to F$: compatibility with restrictions is exactly naturality of the action [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. It is consequently compatible with the same $P$-action and the same abelian sheafification $\mathrm{id}_F$. The unique compatible action in [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] forces it to equal the action constructed in step 2. A module structure extending the given addition is determined by its scalar action, so the module structure is unique.

proof.text: Let $G,G'$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules and $\varphi:\mathrm{forget}(G)\to\mathrm{forget}(G')$ an abelian-sheaf morphism. By step 1 their restricted $P$-actions are the usual $\mathbf Z/n$-actions. Each $\varphi_U$ is additive and therefore $\mathbf Z/n$-linear by clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-zmod-module-structure-killed-by-n]. Naturality of $\varphi$ thus makes it a morphism of presheaves of $P$-modules. Apply the factorization assertion of [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] to the $P$-module presheaf underlying $G$, with abelian sheafification $\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{forget}(G)}$ and target $G'$. Its sheafified $\mathcal O$-module structure equals the original structure on $G$, by the action uniqueness already proved. The resulting $\mathcal O$-linear morphism $G\to G'$ composes with this identity to $\varphi$, so its underlying abelian-sheaf map is exactly $\varphi$. This proves (3).

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), specialized to the constant presheaf of rings Z/n; module definition: Tag 03CW (definition-sheaf-modules). Agent-written application to the coefficient identification used in Tag 03SC (etale-cohomology-theorem-vanishing-affine-curves).

proof.text: By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], a module-sheaf morphism is an abelian-sheaf morphism satisfying linearity, so forgetting the action is injective on morphisms. Step 4 supplies every abelian-sheaf morphism, so the functor is fully faithful. Step 1 shows that every underlying sheaf is killed by $n$, and step 2 realizes every sheaf killed by $n$ as an underlying sheaf. This condition is invariant under an additive isomorphism $f$: $f(ns)=nf(s)$, and the inverse gives the converse. Hence the essential image is the full subcategory asserted in the statement. Finally, an abelian-sheaf isomorphism and its inverse are both module-linear by step 4; their composites are still identities after regarding them as module-sheaf maps, giving the final assertion.
